handback.t:
W6 (SERVE-PERF) is done. The F3 fix works: real `neural-mesh serve --port` throughput on loopback is 2.8x to 14x higher, and replies are byte-identical to round-2 HEAD in all 14 equivalence scenarios. Board entry with the rerun commands is in `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\g6_board_entry.md` (one "### VERIFY REQUEST — W6 — SERVE-PERF" block). I only touched `src/serve.rs` under `src/`; there are no `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` changes, no new crates, and no commits. Every test server uses `--port 0` and the harness asserts it reports a `127.0.0.1:` address.

**Changes in `src/serve.rs` (default behaviour, no reply byte changes)**
- **One write per reply.** Each reply is serialised once into a reused buffer and sent with a single write. The old `writeln!` on the raw `TcpStream` issued about 124 writes per reply.
- **Batched flush.** If the client has more complete request lines already queued, replies are held and sent together (at most 64 KiB). They always go out before the server blocks for input, at EOF, and on `shutdown`. A unit test confirms a lockstep client still gets one write per reply and a 30-request burst gets one write.
- **Parse outside the global lock.** JSON parse, command lookup and field validation now run before taking the `Mutex<Server>`. The per-request allowed-list `Vec` and the array join allocations are gone.
- **Over-long lines are discarded as they stream in.** Lines over 1 MiB are no longer buffered whole; the reply is the same "request line too long". A 200 MB line peaks under 6 MB heap in a unit test.
- **Opt-in, default off:** env `NEURAL_MESH_SERVE_STAT_MS=N` checks the state file at most every N ms instead of before every request. I did not make it default because it changes when an external CLI write is absorbed (never lost). It needs your decision.

**Byte-identity proof (`g6_serve_ab equiv`, about 70 s)**
- It compares the real shipped binaries, not a module copy. The baseline is HEAD 52f936c built by `results/g6_build_baseline.sh` from `git archive`. I did not embed `git show HEAD:src/serve.rs` as a bin module, because `serve.rs` depends on private `main.rs` items.
- The script is 2,839 lines: valid operations, about 85 hand-written error forms, 1,800 fuzzed lines, and lines at the 1 MiB boundary, 3 MiB lines and invalid UTF-8. Roughly 60% of replies are errors.
- It runs 14 scenarios over stdio and TCP: lockstep, one burst, random chunking, byte-at-a-time, EOF mid-line, half-close, shutdown mid-stream, and CLI writes interleaved. Reply bytes, exit codes and final state-file bytes are compared.
- Base-versus-base controls are all deterministic, and a one-byte-changed self-test is detected.
- The rebuilt baseline also matches the original one I used for the numbers.
- In-process there are 6 new serve tests, including a verbatim copy of the old loop compared byte for byte under 1-, 7- and 4093-byte reads.
- Test results: `cargo test --release --lib` 228 passed, 0 failed; `cargo test --release --bin neural-mesh` 19 passed, 1 ignored (the allocation report).

**Decisions/s, medians of 5 reps, base to new (route + feedback per decision)**

| Config | Base | New | Paired ratio (median [min..max]) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TCP lockstep, 1 client | 683 | 5,375 | 7.9x [7.1..9.3] |
| TCP lockstep, 2 clients | 956 | 7,408 | 7.2x |
| TCP lockstep, 4 clients | 1,727 | 6,593 | 4.2x |
| TCP lockstep, 8 clients | 2,517 | 6,915 | 2.8x [2.3..2.95] |
| TCP pipelined 32+32 per write, 1 client | 682 | 9,491 | 13.8x [12.3..15.1] |
| TCP pipelined, 4 clients | 1,749 | 10,281 | 5.9x |
| TCP pipelined, 8 clients | 2,624 | 9,533 | 3.6x |
| stdio, default flush | 7,705 | 8,230 | 1.12x (paired [0.90..1.31]) — not significant |
| stdio, flush off | 11,292 | 15,304 | 1.24x |

- Server CPU per decision at lockstep with 1 client falls from 1,444 µs to 172 µs. Peak working set is unchanged at the default flush (7.5–8.3 MB).
- Allocations per request go from 66.0 to 62.4, about 5.5% fewer, so allocation was never the bottleneck. The remaining allocations sit in `cmd_route`/`cmd_feedback` in `main.rs` and the request `Value` tree, which `serve.rs` cannot change.
- The runs were ABAB-interleaved. A baseline-versus-copy-of-itself control gives a noise floor of roughly ±8% (paired ratios 0.72–1.24).
- Machine load caveat: system CPU was busy a median of 59% (33–97%) in the 250 ms before each run, so absolute numbers are depressed. Trust the paired ratios.

**Negatives**
- **Remaining server cost:** the per-request `fs::metadata` stat on the state file costs about 19 µs on this box. A cheaper Windows call (`GetFileAttributesExW`) only gets it to about 16 µs.
- **Opt-in knob results:** with `NEURAL_MESH_SERVE_STAT_MS=50`, stdio flush-off reaches about 88k decisions/s (5.6x over the default-new build), and TCP lockstep with 8 clients and flush off reaches 41k (4.2x). Those results are in `results/g6_bench_optin_stat50.json`.
- **Flush cost:** each count-triggered flush runs inside the global lock and costs an estimated 3–4 ms. Lockstep with 1 client does 5.4k decisions/s at the default flush versus 6.4k with flush off. Moving it off the request path means restructuring `commit()`, which I did not do.
- **Client scaling is still poor:** at the default flush, going from 1 to 8 clients only goes from 5.4k to 6.9k decisions/s.
- **Not tested:** Linux/macOS, more than 8 clients, the `internal error` panic reply (no input I tried reaches it), and byte equality across concurrent connections (arrival order makes it non-deterministic).

Rerun order matters: run `bash results/g6_build_baseline.sh` first, because it overwrites `release/neural-mesh.exe`, then `cargo build --release --offline --bin neural-mesh --bin g6_serve_ab`, then `g6_serve_ab equiv` and `g6_serve_ab bench`.
